riskTone.label: BULLISH
riskTone.rationale: Cooler US inflation and strong bank earnings drive equity gains; US-Iran tension adds mild offset but risk-on tone dominates.

briefing.briefing: Starting with the currency picture: GBPUSD is up +0.3% today, sitting at the 89th percentile of its 20-day range — meaning sterling is relatively strong right now. Because UK100 and sterling move in opposite directions (a stronger pound makes overseas earnings worth less when converted back to GBP), this acts as a mild headwind [drag] for the index, though the system rates the net FX impact as NEUTRAL given offsetting forces. The dominant regime drivers today are commodities and US risk appetite: Brent crude is up +2.04% (bullish for Shell and BP, two of the biggest index weights), copper is up +1.6% (bullish for miners like Rio and Glencore, which are sensitive to global growth expectations), and European markets are broadly aligned with the UK, with the DAX up +0.36% and EuroStoxx50 up +0.52%. Gilt [UK government bond] yields are slightly lower (-2bp on the 10-year), and long-end stress is absent — no fiscal alarm bells today. The key catalyst from the last few hours is the softer-than-expected US CPI [inflation] print released at 13:30 BST today, which drove Wall Street higher and lifted broad risk appetite (Reuters, ~1–3 hours ago); US-Iran tensions added a mild offset, helping push Brent higher. The directional bias leans BULLISH overall — cooler inflation, strong US bank earnings, rising oil, and rising copper all point in the same direction — but confidence is capped at 5/10 because the ORB already broke DOWNWARD this morning, the 14-day average daily range [typical daily move of ~128 points] has already been exceeded (104% used), and GBP positioning data shows crowded short [most traders are already betting against the pound], which is a contrarian warning that the pound could squeeze higher and cap the index. For the 08:00 ORB trade specifically: today's session has already moved well beyond its normal daily range and broke downward out of the opening range, meaning tomorrow's 08:00 setup is the one to watch — today looks like a stand-aside or news-reaction day rather than a clean mechanical ORB. Event risk: US CPI already printed at 13:30 BST today; look ahead to UK GDP Monthly Estimate on Wednesday at 07:00 BST (two days away, HIGH impact — this drops just before London open so prepare for a gap or early volatility). Key levels: overnight high 10,499.9 and prior day high 10,526.3 are resistance above; overnight low 10,414.8 and ORB low 10,447.4 are support below; current price 10,494.3 sits just inside the overnight range. The one thing to remember: cooler US inflation and rising commodities set a bullish backdrop, but with range already exhausted and the ORB already broken down, tomorrow's open — especially ahead of Wednesday's UK GDP — is the cleaner trade opportunity.
